title: Are Dating and Marriage Worth It
intro: Chapter 10: Are Dating and Marriage Worth It

tips.title: Getting to know more people rather than fixating on just one: You can’t predict compatibility before meeting someone
tips.cost: No cost at all. Spend time getting to know several people instead of obsessing over just one. The hard part is resisting the urge to fixate on a single person.
tips.inPlainWords: Two speed-dating studies asked participants to fill out over 100 questionnaires about their preferences in a partner before any meetings took place. These questionnaires could only reveal how likely someone is to like others in general, and how popular they tend to be — they couldn’t predict whether two specific people would hit it off. Compatibility can only be determined by meeting in person. Therefore, it’s far more worthwhile to get to know multiple people than to bet everything on just one.
tips.benefit: In both speed-dating studies, participants completed more than 100 self-report questionnaires related to partner preferences prior to meeting potential matches. Researchers then applied a random forest model — an algorithm designed to detect patterns — to analyze the data. This model could predict “how likely an individual is to like others overall,” with the questionnaires accounting for 4%–18% of the variance in such tendencies; this represents only a small fraction of the total differences between individuals. It could also predict “how popular an individual tends to be,” explaining 7%–27% of variance. However, it completely failed to predict whether two specific individuals would be compatible; no combination of pre-meeting traits or preferences could be used to forecast their mutual attraction. Earlier, the same research team conducted another speed-dating experiment where participants reported their own ideal preferences — whether they valued physical appearance or financial prospects more. Even this information couldn’t predict how interested they’d be in a particular person during the actual date.
tips.sources: Joel S, Eastwick PW, Finkel EJ (2017). Is romantic desire predictable? Machine learning applied to initial romantic attraction. Psychological Science, 28(10), 1478-1489. <https://doi.org/10.1177/0956797617714580>; Eastwick PW, Finkel EJ (2008). Sex differences in mate preferences revisited: do people know what they initially desire in a romantic partner? Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 94(2), 245-264. <https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-3514.94.2.245>
tips.caveats: Both studies clearly state that compatibility cannot be predicted before meeting someone — they do not claim that all efforts to predict it are futile. Since true compatibility can only be determined by face-to-face interaction, it makes far more sense to invest time in meeting multiple people individually rather than placing all hopes on just one.

tips.title: Stop after a clear refusal: pursuit against a clear 'no' can be stalking, not persistence
tips.cost: No money, and no time beyond the messages you stop sending. The hard part is self-restraint: not sending another message, not waiting outside, not asking friends to plead your case.
tips.inPlainWords: Once someone has clearly said no, further pursuit is not romance. In India, repeatedly following or contacting a woman against her wishes can be stalking under the BNS, 2023, and a threat can be criminal intimidation. Obscene messages fall under the IT Act, 2000, and a court can grant a protection or injunction order. Your intention does not draw the line; the other person's clear refusal does.
tips.benefit: Section 78 of the BNS, 2023 punishes stalking, which includes following a woman, contacting her repeatedly against her wishes, watching her, and monitoring her use of the internet or email; section 77 covers voyeurism. Threats are criminal intimidation under the BNS, 2023, and obscene electronic messages fall under the IT Act, 2000. The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 applies where there is a domestic relationship and can give a protection order. On a campus the UGC sexual-harassment regulations apply, and at a workplace the PoSH Act, 2013. The normal route is a police complaint or an FIR, not an administrative detention.
tips.sources: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Information Technology Act, 2000. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; National Commission for Women. <https://ncw.nic.in/>
tips.caveats: No research shows that persistence wins someone over, and the law does not reward it. A police record can affect a background check, a government job and a professional licence. A false complaint is itself actionable, so keep your own messages and dates. If a refusal is ambiguous, ask once, in writing, and accept the answer.

tips.title: Judging whether someone is interested: focus on actions, not “signals” — who initiates, plans, and follows up
tips.cost: This requires no money or much time. The real challenge is breaking old habits: stop trying to interpret facial expressions and tone, and instead record observable behaviors.
tips.inPlainWords: In one study, 52 pairs of strangers of opposite genders chatted for about 10 minutes, then tried to determine whether each other was flirting. The results showed they were fairly accurate at spotting when no flirting was occurring, but struggled to identify actual flirting. A second experiment using video evaluations reached the same conclusion. Therefore, rather than guessing based on expressions or tone, pay attention to actions: who initiates contact, who schedules future meetings, and whether they follow up when you don’t make the first move.
tips.benefit: Two studies examined how accurately people can recognize flirting. The first involved 52 unrelated male-female pairs conversing for 10–12 minutes; afterward, each participant reported whether they themselves were flirting and whether they believed their partner was. The results indicated that interactions without any flirting were identified more reliably, while those involving actual flirting were harder to detect. The second study used 26 one-minute video clips and 261 observers, yielding similar findings. In short, people can fairly reliably tell when someone is not flirting, but they struggle to detect when flirting is happening.
tips.sources: Hall JA, Xing C, Brooks S (2015). Accurately detecting flirting: error management theory, the traditional sexual script, and flirting base rate. Communication Research, 42(7), 939-958. <https://doi.org/10.1177/0093650214534972>; Perilloux C, Kurzban R (2015). Do men overperceive women's sexual interest? Psychological Science, 26(1), 70-77. <https://doi.org/10.1177/0956797614555727> (Disputing Party)
tips.caveats: This topic remains debated. Some research suggests the issue isn’t that men overestimate women’s sexual intentions, but that women tend to underreport their own intentions on surveys. There is still no consensus on which group judges more accurately. Nevertheless, both viewpoints agree on one point: relying on subtle cues such as facial expressions or tone to infer someone’s thoughts yields poor results. Observable behaviors — such as who initiates contact, plans future meetings, and follows up without prompting — are far more reliable indicators.

tips.title: Whether a relationship is good or not depends mainly on how you feel within it, not on your partner’s attributes.
tips.cost: There is no monetary cost, nor does it require much time. The real challenge lies in shifting your perspective: put aside your checklist of ideal partner traits and instead focus on how you interact with each other.
tips.inPlainWords: The best indicator of a healthy relationship is your own feelings toward it, not your partner’s qualifications. For instance, whether you perceive your partner as attentive and appreciative of you, or how often you argue. Your personal feelings carry two to four times more weight than what your partner says about the relationship. However, no questionnaire can reliably predict whether the relationship will improve or deteriorate over time.
tips.benefit: A machine learning analysis of data from 29 laboratories and 43 longitudinal paired datasets — meaning data collected from the same couples over time — found that the strongest predictors of relationship quality all stem from each partner’s own perceptions of the relationship: their sense of their partner’s commitment, appreciation, sexual satisfaction, and contentment; as well as the frequency of conflicts. Among individual-level factors, life satisfaction, negative emotions, depression, and attachment styles (both avoidant and anxious) also play a role. At the start of these studies, these relationship-related factors could explain up to 45% of the variation in relationship quality between different couples; by the end of the studies, this figure dropped to 18%. Crucially, the predictive power of self-reported relationship perceptions is two to four times greater than that of perceptions reported by partners. Adding individual differences and partner-reported data to self-reported perceptions yields no additional predictive value.
tips.sources: Joel S, Eastwick PW, Allison CJ, et al. (2020). Machine learning uncovers the most robust self-report predictors of relationship quality across 43 longitudinal couples studies. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, 117(32), 19061-19071. <https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1917036117>
tips.caveats: This same research also found that no set of self-reported questionnaire items can reliably forecast whether a relationship will improve or worsen during the study period. Therefore, while gauging your own feelings about the relationship is far more accurate than cross-checking your partner against a checklist of ideal traits, it still cannot predict the relationship’s future trajectory. For a deeper look at how relationship quality ties to physical health, see Section 17 of this chapter, which frames relationship health as a component of overall well-being.

tips.title: To build closeness, have two people take turns answering a series of progressively deeper questions — no script needed
tips.cost: No cost involved. It takes 45 minutes to complete.
tips.inPlainWords: Pair two strangers up and have them take turns answering 36 questions grouped into three levels of depth. After 45 minutes, their sense of closeness is noticeably higher than in a control group that simply chatted for the same amount of time. What drives this effect is the act of taking turns to share honest thoughts at increasing levels of depth, not any pre-planned conversational script. Keep in mind this measure only captures short-term closeness, and does not guarantee the development of a long-term relationship.
tips.benefit: This method pairs two unfamiliar people to answer 36 questions in total, arranged in three tiers of increasing depth. The questions range from “Who is the person you’d most like to invite for dinner?” to “When was the last time you cried in front of someone?” After 45 minutes, the participants report a higher sense of closeness compared to those who only chatted for the same duration. Their reported closeness also exceeds the average rating college students give to their closest real-life relationships.
tips.sources: Aron A, Melinat E, Aron EN, Vallone RD, Bator RJ (1997). The experimental generation of interpersonal closeness: a procedure and some preliminary findings. Personality and Social Psychology Bulletin, 23(4), 363-377. <https://doi.org/10.1177/0146167297234003>
tips.caveats: Only one experiment has been conducted so far, with college students as participants. It measures short-term closeness only, not whether a lasting relationship can form. The core mechanism at work here is that closeness grows when two people take turns sharing genuine personal details at progressively deeper levels — rather than relying on scripts, tricks or one-sided efforts. The key takeaway for practical use is to “share something honest about yourself, then ask a similarly personal question back”, and make sure both parties get a turn to do so.

tips.title: Long-distance relationships aren’t worse than local ones — the real challenge comes in the first three months after moving in together
tips.cost: There are travel expenses to consider, plus the time spent traveling back and forth. Couples see each other far less often than those living in the same city, making it difficult to maintain the relationship over the long term without regular contact.
tips.inPlainWords: Long-distance relationships actually tend to be more stable while the couple remains apart, since seeing each other infrequently allows each person to idealize the other. The real difficulty emerges only after they move in together. Data shows that roughly half of long-distance couples eventually transition to living locally, while the other half end their relationship while still apart. Among those who reunite, one-third break up within three months of moving together.
tips.benefit: Two separate studies reach the same conclusion: long-distance relationships are generally more stable than local ones while the couple remains separated. This stability stems from a significantly higher degree of idealization — meaning each partner tends to view the other more favorably than reality warrants. The studies measured factors such as idealized distortion, romantic love, relationship memories, and perceived similarity. Moreover, the less frequently couples meet, the more positively they tend to view each other. However, this stability holds only while they remain apart; once they live in the same city, long-distance couples are far more likely to split up. One longitudinal study found that about half of long-distance couples eventually moved in together, while the other half ended their relationship while still apart. Of those who reunited, one-third broke up within three months of living together. The longer the intervals between visits while apart, and the greater the degree of idealization, the less stable the relationship tends to be after reuniting.
tips.sources: Stafford L, Merolla AJ, Castle JD (2006). When long-distance dating partners become geographically close. Journal of Social and Personal Relationships, 23(6), 901-919. <https://doi.org/10.1177/0265407506070472>; Stafford L, Merolla AJ (2007). Idealization, reunions, and stability in long-distance dating relationships. Journal of Social and Personal Relationships, 24(1), 37-54. <https://doi.org/10.1177/0265407507072578>; Dargie E et al. (2015). Journal of Sex & Marital Therapy, 41(2), 181-202. <https://doi.org/10.1080/0092623X.2013.864367> (Remarks on the off-site study)
tips.caveats: These findings are based on romantic relationships among American university students, excluding married couples, and date back to an earlier era; thus, absolute percentages should not be applied directly to current populations. Another study surveyed 717 long-distance couples and 425 local couples, finding only minimal differences in overall relationship quality between the two groups. Ultimately, relationship success depends on the individuals involved and the nature of their bond itself, rather than physical distance. The key takeaway is this: do not assume that long-distance relationships are destined to fail. Instead, couples should prepare for the initial months after reuniting, when personal independence diminishes, mutual understanding increases, and conflicts or jealousy are more likely to arise.

tips.title: Read the numbers behind 'marriage rate' and 'divorce rate' before you believe a claim about marriage
tips.cost: Nothing but a few minutes. India has no single national marriage register, so check what a figure actually counts before you repeat it.
tips.inPlainWords: India does not publish one national count of marriages and divorces. Marriages are registered under state rules made under the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, the Special Marriage Act, 1954 and the personal laws, while the Registrar General's Civil Registration System covers births and deaths, not marriages. A 'divorce rate' quoted online is often just the number of divorces divided by the number of marriages in the same year. Those are different groups of people, so the ratio is not the chance that a marriage ends.
tips.benefit: A crude marriage rate divides the number of marriages in a year by the whole population, including children and unmarried people; a divorce-to-marriage ratio divides one year's divorces by that year's marriages. Neither tells you what happens to a given couple. Answering that needs a cohort followed for decades, and India does not publish one. The usable Indian sources are the Civil Registration System reports, the National Family Health Survey and the National Statistical Office surveys; read the definition before the headline.
tips.sources: Registrar General of India, Civil Registration System. <https://crsorgi.gov.in/>; Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Special Marriage Act, 1954. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation. <https://www.mospi.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: Under-registration and differences between states make a national comparison misleading, and a high ratio can simply reflect many marriages in the past or few marriages this year. Do not use a ratio to predict your own marriage, and do not accept a percentage from a screenshot without the year and the definition.

tips.title: Accounting for health benefits while adjusting for observational data
tips.cost: There is no cost in money or time. Just keep in mind that these figures reflect a lower mortality rate among married individuals — this simply means both conditions occur together, not that marriage itself extends life expectancy.
tips.inPlainWords: Over a given period, married people have a roughly 12% lower chance of dying compared to unmarried individuals, while those who have never married face a roughly 24% higher risk. However, this merely shows a correlation between marital status and mortality; it does not prove that marriage directly causes longer life. People who are healthier, wealthier, and more socially active are both more likely to marry and more likely to live longer.
tips.benefit: One meta-analysis of older adults pooled results from multiple studies, covering 53 comparisons and over 250,000 participants. It found that the relative risk of all-cause mortality for married versus unmarried individuals was RR 0.88, with a 95% confidence interval of 0.85–0.91. In other words, married people had a roughly 12% lower probability of dying during the study period. Among widowed individuals, this figure rose to 1.11; for divorced or separated persons, it was 1.16; and for those never married, it was 1.11 — indicating respective increases of about 11%, 16%, and 11% in mortality risk. No significant gender differences emerged. Under the most conservative estimates, the RR still came out at 0.94, reflecting a reduction of only around 6%. Another meta-analysis compared never-married individuals with married ones, drawing on 95 separate studies and over 500 million participants. It reported a hazard ratio of 1.24 (95% CI 1.19–1.30), meaning unmarried people faced roughly 24% higher mortality risk over the same timeframe; this gap narrowed with age. A further gender-specific meta-analysis examined 21 studies involving more than 7,890,000 individuals: across both sexes, unmarried status correlated with higher rates of overall mortality, cancer-related death, and cardiovascular death. Among men, the disparity was especially pronounced for cardiovascular and overall mortality; unmarried men also faced a 31% higher risk of stroke and a 9% higher risk of all-cause death compared to unmarried women.
tips.sources: Manzoli L, et al. (2007). Marital status and mortality in the elderly: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Soc Sci Med 64:77–94. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.socscimed.2006.08.031>; Roelfs DJ, et al. (2011). The rising relative risk of mortality for singles: meta-analysis and meta-regression. Am J Epidemiol 174(4):379–389. <https://doi.org/10.1093/aje/kwr111>; Wang Y, et al. (2020). Sex differences in the association between marital status and the risk of cardiovascular, cancer, and all-cause mortality: a systematic review and meta-analysis of 7,881,040 individuals. Glob Health Res Policy 5:4. <https://doi.org/10.1186/s41256-020-00133-8>
tips.caveats: The controversy stems from the fact that married individuals tend to be healthier, wealthier, and more socially engaged — factors that independently contribute to longer life. All three meta-analyses relied on observational data collected from existing populations; no controlled experiments or randomized groups were used. The authors themselves acknowledged potential publication bias and methodological limitations. Roelfs also noted that studies employing more rigorous methods tended to report smaller differences between marital groups.

tips.title: Agree how unpaid work will be shared before marriage: no law will divide it for you afterwards
tips.cost: No money. Spend an hour or two before marriage agreeing who does the cooking, cleaning, childcare and elder care, and how that changes when a child arrives or a parent falls ill. The hard part is the conversation, not the cost.
tips.inPlainWords: India's Time Use Survey, 2019, run by the National Statistical Office, found that women spend far more of the day on unpaid domestic work and care-giving than men. The survey did not report the split by marital status, so there is no official figure for how much housework rises after marriage. The law does not divide housework; it matters later, when a court fixes maintenance or when one spouse has given up a career.
tips.benefit: The Time Use Survey, 2019 measured unpaid domestic services and care-giving separately for men and women and found a large gap; read the report tables rather than a summary. The legal consequences of that gap appear at separation: maintenance and alimony under the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 and the Special Marriage Act, 1954, interim maintenance and litigation expenses, and monetary relief under the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005. A written household agreement has no statutory force, but it records the intention and can be evidence later.
tips.sources: Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation, Time Use Survey. <https://www.mospi.gov.in/>; Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>
tips.caveats: A national average says nothing about your household, and a couple may choose any division they like. What matters is that the arrangement is stated, reviewed when circumstances change, and not assumed. If one partner stops paid work to care for children or parents, record that decision and keep the money arrangements in both names where possible: joint accounts, nominations and property documents.

tips.title: Check what Indian law says about money and property in marriage, then decide whether a written agreement helps
tips.cost: No money to read the rules. A written agreement costs what a lawyer charges, and a registered deed costs stamp duty and registration fees set by the state. The real work is an honest conversation about money before marriage.
tips.inPlainWords: India has no community of property: nothing says that everything earned during a marriage belongs to both spouses. Property generally belongs to the person in whose name it is held, and a Hindu woman's property is her own absolutely. What marriage does create is maintenance, a right of residence in the shared household, and rights in a joint family's coparcenary property. A written agreement can record intentions, but it cannot sign away maintenance or a child's rights.
tips.benefit: The Hindu Succession Act, 1956 makes a daughter a coparcener (section 6), makes a Hindu woman's property her absolute property (section 14) and lists a widow among Class I heirs (section 8). The Indian Succession Act, 1925 governs wills and the succession of Christians and Parsis, and Muslim succession follows personal law. A marriage under the Special Marriage Act, 1954 takes its succession from the Indian Succession Act. A Hindu marriage is dissolved under the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, with maintenance and a share of jointly held property. A prenuptial agreement has no statutory basis in India and courts have taken differing views, so it is evidence of intention, not a substitute for statutory rights.
tips.sources: Hindu Succession Act, 1956. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Indian Succession Act, 1925. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Special Marriage Act, 1954. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>
tips.caveats: Goa, whose family law comes from the Portuguese era, is the main exception and recognises a form of joint property. A gift from a relative, including a spouse, is generally not taxed as income under the Income-tax Act, 1961, but a transfer of immovable property needs a registered deed and stamp duty. Keep the title, the payment trail and the loan documents in both names where you want both to own. Do not assume a clause waiving maintenance will be enforced.

tips.title: When parents pay for a house, say at the time of payment whether the money is a loan or a gift
tips.cost: No cost for the note itself. A loan agreement or a gift deed costs what a lawyer charges, and a deed for immovable property needs stamp duty and registration. Write it on the day the money moves, not after a dispute.
tips.inPlainWords: When parents pay for a house, the money can be a gift or a loan, and the difference matters if the marriage later breaks down. A gift to a son or daughter is that child's property, but a house bought in the couple's joint names belongs to both. A loan is repayable to the parents and is proved by the transfer, the agreement and any repayments. Put the choice in writing, sign it, and have both spouses sign if it is a loan.
tips.benefit: Indian courts look at the source of the funds, the intention of the parents and the conduct of the parties when a house is claimed at divorce, and a document made at the time is far stronger than one produced after separation. A gift from a parent, being a relative, is not treated as the child's income under section 56(2)(x) of the Income-tax Act, 1961. A gift of immovable property needs a registered instrument under the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 read with the Registration Act, 1908. For a loan, record the amount, the date, the interest if any and the repayment terms.
tips.sources: Transfer of Property Act, 1882. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Registration Act, 1908. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Income-tax Act, 1961. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>
tips.caveats: A document created after the marriage has failed is viewed with suspicion, so date it and keep the bank trail from the parents' account. If the house is in the son's name alone, the wife may still have a right of residence in the shared household under the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005. If both spouses pay and both names are on the deed, a private note between parent and child cannot undo the title. Take advice before registering anything.

tips.title: A large loan in your spouse's name is not automatically your debt: check whether you signed or guaranteed it
tips.cost: No cost. Do not sign as a co-borrower or a guarantor unless you are willing to pay the whole loan, and do not confirm the debt in a message. The hard part is staying calm when a recovery agent calls.
tips.inPlainWords: In India a debt is yours if you signed the loan agreement, stood as a guarantor, held the account jointly, or mortgaged property you own. A loan in your spouse's name alone is their contract, and a default does not appear on your credit report unless you are a co-borrower. If the loan is secured on a house you jointly own, the lender can enforce the mortgage. Marriage does not make you liable, and silence does not protect you either.
tips.benefit: The Indian Contract Act, 1872 makes only the parties to a contract liable on it; a surety's liability is co-extensive with the principal debtor's (section 128), and a material variation of the contract without the surety's consent can discharge the surety (section 133). A Hindu undivided family's debt can bind coparceners in limited circumstances, which is one reason to keep business borrowing separate from family property. Where a loan is secured, the lender's remedy is against the mortgaged property under the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, whether or not you signed.
tips.sources: Indian Contract Act, 1872. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Transfer of Property Act, 1882. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Reserve Bank of India. <https://www.rbi.org.in/>
tips.caveats: A joint account, a joint home loan or a co-signed guarantee is the usual way a spouse's debt becomes yours. Check your credit report with each bureau to see which loans name you, and ask the lender for the guarantee document if you are shown as a surety. If a recovery agent threatens you, complain to the lender's grievance officer and to the RBI under its Integrated Ombudsman Scheme. A loan taken for a business you never benefited from is still yours if you signed.

tips.title: Marriage registration in India: the documents and the notice depend on the law you marry under
tips.cost: The fee is small and set by the state. A lawyer is optional for a straightforward registration. Do not pay an agent for a 'guaranteed' date.
tips.inPlainWords: A Hindu marriage can be registered under the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955; a marriage under the Special Marriage Act, 1954 needs a notice to the marriage officer and a 30-day window for objections. Documents usually include age proof, address proof, photographs and witnesses. There is no household-register requirement, and no fee should be paid to an agent to 'fix' a date.
tips.benefit: The Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 (section 8) and the state registration rules govern registration. The Special Marriage Act, 1954 requires a notice and a certificate; the notice is public and allows objections. The Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006 sets the minimum age at 18 for a woman and 21 for a man. A registrar may ask for proof of age and address, but not a household register. A marriage solemnised under a religious law can be registered under that law.
tips.sources: Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Special Marriage Act, 1954. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>
tips.caveats: A marriage registration is not the same as a marriage; the ceremony and the applicable law come first. A notice under the Special Marriage Act is public, so a person in a hurry may prefer a different route. Keep the certificate safe; it is needed for a passport and a visa.

tips.title: A premarital health check is voluntary in India: if something serious is found, disclose it before the wedding
tips.cost: A check-up at a government hospital or health centre is cheap or free; a private panel costs what the laboratory charges. It takes part of a day. The hard part is saying the result out loud.
tips.inPlainWords: India has no mandatory premarital medical examination and no duty in law to produce a fitness certificate; testing is voluntary. If a serious condition is concealed, the other person's remedy is not an automatic annulment: it depends on the condition and on whether the concealment goes to consent. A marriage can be annulled for impotence, unsoundness of mind, fraud or force, and a marriage under the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 can be dissolved for mental disorder or a venereal disease in a communicable form.
tips.benefit: Sections 11 and 12 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 deal with void and voidable marriages, and the voidable grounds include impotence, unsoundness of mind at the time of marriage, and fraud or force. Section 13 allows divorce for adultery, cruelty, desertion, conversion, mental disorder, venereal disease in a communicable form, renunciation and seven years' absence. The Special Marriage Act, 1954 has parallel provisions. Testing itself runs on consent: the HIV and AIDS (Prevention and Control) Act, 2017 requires informed consent for an HIV test and protects confidentiality.
tips.sources: Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Special Marriage Act, 1954. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; HIV and AIDS (Prevention and Control) Act, 2017. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. <https://mohfw.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: Doctors and laboratories owe confidentiality, and a result shared with a fiancé is a disclosure the person chooses unless a law requires it. There is no Indian statute that gives a one-year window to annul a marriage for a concealed illness, so do not expect that remedy. If you learn of a serious condition, get medical advice on treatment and transmission and decide together; a court case is slower, costlier and less certain than a conversation.

tips.title: Count the cost of leaving before you marry: mutual consent needs a wait, and a contested divorce needs a ground
tips.cost: Court fees are set by the state and lawyer fees are yours alone; legal aid is free through NALSA if you qualify. The real cost is time: a mutual-consent divorce has a waiting period, and a contested one can run for years.
tips.inPlainWords: There are two routes. A divorce by mutual consent under the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, the Special Marriage Act, 1954 or the Divorce Act, 1869 needs a year of living apart, a joint petition, and a second motion after a cooling-off period of six months, which a court can waive. A contested divorce needs a ground such as adultery, cruelty, desertion for two years, conversion, mental disorder or venereal disease. Courts try mediation first.
tips.benefit: Section 13B of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 requires the spouses to have lived separately for a year and provides for a decree on a joint petition; in Amardeep Singh v Harveen Kaur (2017) the Supreme Court held that the six-month cooling-off period can be waived where the parties have settled everything. Sections 13 and 13(2) list the contested grounds, including the special grounds available to a wife. The Special Marriage Act, 1954 and the Divorce Act, 1869 have their own grounds and their own mutual-consent routes. For Muslims, the Dissolution of Muslim Marriages Act, 1939 provides grounds, and instant triple talaq is void and an offence under the 2019 Act.
tips.sources: Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Special Marriage Act, 1954. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Divorce Act, 1869. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Dissolution of Muslim Marriages Act, 1939. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; National Legal Services Authority. <https://nalsa.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: Irretrievable breakdown is not a statutory ground in India, although the Supreme Court has dissolved marriages under Article 142 in rare cases. A separation agreement, a waiver of maintenance or a custody clause is not automatically binding if it defeats the child's welfare or a statutory right. Keep the marriage certificate, the separation date and the financial records; they decide which route is open and how long it takes.

tips.title: Make a separate tally for the benefits to your elders when they get married — don’t mix it with your own records.
tips.cost: No cost at all. Just draw two columns on paper. One column lists the benefits that go to you from this marriage — you can calculate those using the earlier sections. The other column lists the benefits that go to your elders: peace of mind, social prestige, and an end to pressure to marry. The hard part is keeping the elders’ column separate and not merging it with yours.
tips.inPlainWords: The benefits your elders gain — peace of mind, social standing, and relief from marriage pressure — are very real. But they won’t automatically translate into better health outcomes or improved relationship quality for you. Meanwhile, the time costs, financial outlays, and exit costs all fall squarely on your shoulders. By drawing two columns on paper and assigning each benefit to the right party, you can instantly see whether this arrangement is worth it for you.
tips.benefit: The benefits your elders receive are genuine. Yet they do not automatically become gains in your own health (see Section 8) or relationship quality (see Section 4; how good your relationship is depends on your own feelings). All time costs (Section 9), financial expenses (Sections 10–12), and exit costs (Section 15) must be borne by you. Once you keep separate records, you can easily judge whether marrying “as a duty” offers any real value for you.
tips.sources: author’s experience, method suggestions; see the previous items in this section for the data part; Ministry of Women and Child Development. <https://wcd.gov.in/>; National Legal Services Authority. <https://nalsa.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: You may also treat the elders’ share of benefits as a major factor in your calculations; how you weigh it is entirely up to you. A fill‑in worksheet is available at [docs/is-marriage-financially-worth-it.md](../docs/is-marriage-financially-worth-it.md).

tips.title: Treating relationship quality as a health factor: focus on the issue, not the person — avoid insults and sarcasm
tips.cost: No cost at all. When arguing, stick to the current issue only; do not insult, mock, or bring up past grievances. The real challenge is keeping your mouth in check when angry.
tips.inPlainWords: Couples with a good relationship tend to be healthier and have a lower risk of mortality. This link is relatively weak — comparable to how diet affects health. In one experiment, wounds on partners who remained hostile during arguments healed at only 60% of the rate seen in couples who stayed calm.
tips.benefit: This conclusion comes from a meta-analysis of 126 studies involving over 72,000 participants. Higher marital quality correlates with better health, with correlation coefficients ranging from 0.07 to 0.21 (where 0 means no link and 1 means perfect alignment). The strongest association is with reduced mortality, at r = 0.11. Additionally, hostile arguments lead to a weaker cardiovascular response, with r = -0.13. These effects are modest, similar in magnitude to those linked to dietary habits. In another controlled experiment, 42 healthy couples were hospitalized twice for 24 hours each: once for supportive conversation and once to discuss a contentious issue. After the argument, wounds healed more slowly; couples displaying greater hostility saw healing at just 60% of the rate seen in low‑hostility pairs. The next morning, their blood showed higher levels of inflammatory markers such as IL‑6 and tumor necrosis factor.
tips.sources: Robles TF, Slatcher RB, Trombello JM, McGinn MM (2014). Marital quality and health: a meta-analytic review. Psychological Bulletin. <https://doi.org/10.1037/a0031859>; Kiecolt-Glaser JK et al. (2005). Hostile marital interactions, proinflammatory cytokine production, and wound healing. Archives of General Psychiatry. <https://doi.org/10.1001/archpsyc.62.12.1377>
tips.caveats: The B rating reflects that most included studies were observational and lacked controlled groups, making it hard to determine whether poor relationships cause health problems or vice versa. Even after adjusting for age and income, some associations persisted. The original study also notes potential publication bias. Gender differences were not evident in studies that compared men and women. No meta‑analysis directly compares mortality rates between couples in bad marriages and those who remain unmarried; thus the claim that “bad marriages are worse for health than staying single” remains a hypothesis. The wound‑healing experiments involved only 42 couples. The advice “focus on the issue, not the person — avoid insults and sarcasm” is derived from observed hostile behaviors in those studies; no research has directly tested this approach. If arguments persist despite these efforts, couples may consider couple therapy (see Section 20). Physical violence, chronic insults, or threats go beyond communication issues and constitute domestic abuse (see Section 8, Item 43). For guidance on whether to leave a relationship and the associated costs, see Section 15 on exit costs.

tips.title: Same-sex partners should sign a will, a power of attorney and a nomination while both are well: Indian law gives a partner no automatic right to decide or to inherit
tips.cost: A will can be written by hand at no cost; a power of attorney, a nomination with each bank and fund, and a notarised document cost what a lawyer and a notary charge. The set takes a couple of afternoons. The hard part is talking about illness and death.
tips.inPlainWords: India does not recognise a marriage or a civil union between two people of the same sex, so a partner is not a spouse: not a Class I heir, not a next of kin for a hospital, and not entitled to a family pension. Four documents close most of the gap: a will naming the partner, a power of attorney for money and property, nominations in bank, provident fund and insurance accounts, and a written authority the hospital will accept.
tips.benefit: The Indian Succession Act, 1925 lets a person leave property by will to anyone, and section 63 requires the will to be signed and attested by two witnesses. A power of attorney under the Powers of Attorney Act, 1882 lets the partner act on property and financial matters, and one dealing with immovable property is normally registered. Nominations under the Employees' Provident Funds Scheme and in insurance policies pay the nominee. The Mental Healthcare Act, 2017 allows an advance directive and a nominated representative for mental-health decisions. The Supreme Court recognised a limited form of advance medical directive in Common Cause v Union of India (2018), and declined to recognise same-sex marriage in Supriyo v Union of India (2023).
tips.sources: Indian Succession Act, 1925. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Powers of Attorney Act, 1882. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Mental Healthcare Act, 2017. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Employees' Provident Fund Organisation. <https://www.epfo.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: There is no 'voluntary guardianship agreement' in Indian law; the nearest instruments are the will, the power of attorney, the Mental Healthcare Act advance directive and the nomination. Hospitals differ in what they accept at the desk, so ask your regular hospital what it needs and keep a signed letter with the partner's phone number. For organ donation, the Transplantation of Human Organs and Tissues Act, 1994 defines 'near relative' narrowly, so a partner may need the authorisation committee. Review the will after any change in assets or family.

tips.title: Do not marry while hiding your orientation, and do not treat a marriage of convenience as a short-term arrangement: in law it is a real marriage
tips.cost: No money to decide honestly. The cost of a marriage entered to satisfy family is years of a life you did not choose, and a divorce at the end of it. The hard part is refusing the pressure now.
tips.inPlainWords: Indian law does not recognise a marriage between two people of the same sex, and it does not annul a marriage because one spouse is gay or lesbian. Concealment may be argued as fraud or cruelty, but the outcome depends on the court; the reliable exit is divorce. A marriage of convenience is a real marriage: maintenance, property, a child's legitimacy and succession all follow from it, and marrying again while it subsists is bigamy.
tips.benefit: The Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 and the Special Marriage Act, 1954 set the conditions for a valid marriage and the grounds for divorce, and neither list includes sexual orientation. Section 12 of the Hindu Marriage Act allows annulment for impotence, unsoundness of mind, fraud or force, and a court may treat a fundamental deception about the marriage as fraud, but the case law is not uniform. Maintenance is available under sections 24 and 25 of that Act and under section 144 of the BNSS, 2023. Bigamy is an offence under the BNS, 2023. The Supreme Court decriminalised consensual same-sex sex in Navtej Singh Johar (2018) but declined to recognise same-sex marriage in Supriyo v Union of India (2023).
tips.sources: Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Special Marriage Act, 1954. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; National Legal Services Authority. <https://nalsa.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: Compensation for emotional distress is not a standard remedy in an Indian divorce; a court may order costs, maintenance and a share of joint property, and may treat the deception as cruelty. A child born of the marriage is legitimate whatever happens to the marriage. If both spouses have partners of their own, those partners get nothing from the marriage, so their property and care arrangements need separate documents.

tips.title: When a relationship is stuck in endless arguments and silent treatment, couples therapy can help — waiting alone rarely does
tips.cost: Couples therapy comes at a cost. Fees are charged per session and vary by location and clinic; no exact figures are provided here. Typically, participants attend weekly sessions over a period of about eight months. The main challenge is that both partners must attend regularly and see it through to the end.
tips.inPlainWords: Couples who attend therapy together tend to report significantly higher relationship satisfaction — roughly 70% experience noticeable improvement. In contrast, couples who simply wait without any intervention show little to no change. However, these benefits tend to fade over time: after five years, about half of those who sought therapy still report clear gains, while roughly a quarter end up separated or divorced.
tips.benefit: A 2020 meta-analysis examined 58 studies involving 2,092 couples. After completing therapy, the average change in relationship satisfaction was g = 1.12 (95% CI: 0.92–1.31), which researchers consider a large effect size. g is an effect size measure; see the glossary for details. For couples who only waited without therapy, the same period yielded g = 0.12 (−0.04 to 0.29), indicating virtually no improvement. The greater the initial dissatisfaction, the larger the subsequent gain. Another review from 2012 reported that 70% of couples receiving therapy showed positive outcomes. One randomized trial followed 134 long‑married couples with serious conflicts; after eight months of two different behavioral therapy programs, satisfaction improved by d = 0.90 and d = 0.71 respectively. Five years later, 50.0% and 45.9% of those couples still showed clinically meaningful improvement. At the same time, 25.7% and 27.9% had separated or divorced.
tips.sources: Roddy MK, Walsh LM, Rothman K, Hatch SG, Doss BD (2020). Meta-analysis of couple therapy: effects across outcomes, designs, timeframes, and other moderators. Journal of Consulting and Clinical Psychology, 88(7), 583-596. <https://doi.org/10.1037/ccp0000514>; Lebow JL, Chambers AL, Christensen A, Johnson SM (2012). Research on the treatment of couple distress. Journal of Marital and Family Therapy, 38(1), 145-168. Christensen A, Atkins DC, Baucom B, Yi J (2010). Marital status and satisfaction five years following a Randomized clinical trial comparing traditional versus integrative behavioral couple therapy. Journal of Consulting and Clinical Psychology, 78(2), 225-235. <https://doi.org/10.1037/a0018132>; Rathgeber M, Bürkner PC, Schiller EM, Holling H (2019). The efficacy of emotionally focused couples therapy and behavioral couples therapy: a meta-analysis. Journal of Marital and Family Therapy, 45(3), 447-463. <https://doi.org/10.1111/jmft.12336> (Disputant); Shadish WR, Baldwin SA (2003). Meta-analysis of MFT interventions. Journal of Marital and Family Therapy, 29(4), 547-570. <https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1752-0606.2003.tb01694.x> (disputing party); Karakurt G, Whiting K, van Esch C, Bolen SD, Calabrese JR (2016). Couples therapy for intimate partner violence: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Journal of Marital and Family Therapy, 42(4), 567-583. <https://doi.org/10.1111/jmft.12178>
tips.caveats: The main controversy concerns how long these benefits actually last. Another meta-analysis limited to randomized trials found g = 0.60 right after therapy and g = 0.44 after six months; by twelve months only one behavioral therapy approach retained any measurable effect, with g = 0.06 — essentially negligible. A broader review of 20 meta-analyses concluded that clinically meaningful improvement occurs in 40% to 50% of participants. The figures “70% improvement” and “40–50% clinically meaningful improvement” refer to different criteria and should not be directly compared. The five‑year trial lacked a control group of couples receiving no treatment, so it is unclear whether divorce rates rose or fell. You can inquire at psychiatric or psychology departments of hospitals about available couples therapy programs. If seeking outside a hospital, verify the practitioner’s credentials and training. Couples experiencing domestic violence should not begin therapy together. A 2016 meta‑analysis noted that its conclusions apply only to mild‑to‑moderate conflicts where both partners occasionally engage in physical altercations; it does not cover situations dominated by controlling or severely harmful behavior. There is also concern that returning home after therapy might increase the risk of retaliation. If you have been physically abused, see Section 8, Item 43. For advice on how to talk during arguments, see Section 17; for guidance on whether to end the relationship, see Section 15. The primary beneficiaries of therapy are both you and your spouse.

tips.title: A wedding alone can be a valid marriage in India, but register it: without a certificate, proving it costs years
tips.cost: Registration fees are small and set by the state. A wedding without a certificate costs nothing at the time and a great deal later, when a pension, a succession certificate or a visa needs proof.
tips.inPlainWords: Under the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 a marriage is complete on the ceremony, and registration is evidence rather than the source of validity; a marriage under the Special Marriage Act, 1954 is different, because the marriage officer solemnises and registers it. If your partner dies and you were never registered, you are still a widow or widower in law, but you must prove the marriage with photographs, invitations, witnesses and joint records, which a pension office, a bank or a court may not accept quickly.
tips.benefit: Section 7 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 sets out the ceremonies and section 8 provides for registration; section 8(5) says the validity of a Hindu marriage is not affected by the omission to register it. The Hindu Succession Act, 1956 makes a widow a Class I heir. For Christians and Parsis the Indian Succession Act, 1925 governs succession, and for Christians the Indian Christian Marriage Act, 1872 governs the ceremony. For Muslims the nikah is recorded in the nikahnama under state registration rules. Registration is the cheapest evidence you will ever buy.
tips.sources: Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Special Marriage Act, 1954. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Hindu Succession Act, 1956. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Indian Succession Act, 1925. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>
tips.caveats: An unregistered partner is not automatically excluded from inheritance, but every claim becomes a proof problem. Children of a void or voidable marriage are legitimate under section 16 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. A live-in partner is not a spouse: the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 can protect a relationship in the nature of marriage, but it does not create inheritance rights. Register while both of you can sign.

tips.title: If a spouse spends large sums on someone outside the marriage, follow the money: India has no joint property to divide, so the remedy depends on whose name the asset is in
tips.cost: A lawyer and court fees, and court fees are not recovered from the losing side. Tracing the money takes weeks: bank statements, UPI records, card bills and the platform's statements. Prevention is cheaper: keep one account in your own name and know where the family money sits.
tips.inPlainWords: Indian law does not treat a couple's earnings as common property, so there is no 'divide the property during the marriage' remedy of the kind some countries have. What you can do depends on the asset: if a house or account is in your name or jointly held, you can sue for a declaration, an injunction or partition; if the spending is draining the family, it is a factor when a court fixes maintenance. Money paid to a fraudster on a livestream can also be reported as cyber fraud.
tips.benefit: Maintenance and interim relief are available under sections 24 and 25 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 and the parallel provisions of the Special Marriage Act, 1954, and under section 144 of the BNSS, 2023; a court can take a spouse's spending and concealment into account when fixing the amount. A transfer of property made to defeat a person's right can be challenged as a fraudulent transfer under section 53 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882. The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 provides monetary relief and compensation. Where the recipient is a fraudster, report it at cybercrime.gov.in or on 1930.
tips.sources: Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Transfer of Property Act, 1882. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal. <https://cybercrime.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: A gift to a third party is not automatically recoverable by the other spouse, because the money may never have been the other spouse's property. If the account is joint, the bank's records decide who withdrew what. Collect the statements yourself; a court will not go fishing for you. Do not confront the recipient directly, and do not sign a settlement before you have the numbers.

tips.title: When you divorce with young children, put custody, monthly support and the exact visiting days into the decree
tips.cost: A settlement inside a mutual-consent divorce costs the drafting; a contested custody fight costs years and fees. Court fees are set by the state, and legal aid is free through NALSA if you qualify. The expensive part is vagueness.
tips.inPlainWords: Custody in India is decided by the child's welfare, not by the parents' wishes, and there is no fixed percentage for monthly support: a court looks at the child's needs, the parents' income and the standard of living. A child under five is ordinarily with the mother. Write the amount, the payment date, the bank account, the handover hours, the holidays and the school fees into the agreement, because enforcing a vague clause means a fresh case.
tips.benefit: The Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act, 1956 gives the mother custody of a child below five years in the ordinary case, and the Guardians and Wards Act, 1890 makes the child's welfare the paramount consideration. Section 26 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 lets the court make custody and maintenance orders, and section 144 of the BNSS, 2023 provides a quick maintenance order for a wife and children. A child's own wish is a factor, not a rule tied to a fixed age. Maintenance can be varied when circumstances change.
tips.sources: Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act, 1956. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Guardians and Wards Act, 1890. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; National Legal Services Authority. <https://nalsa.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: A clause that one parent pays nothing is not the end of the matter: a court can order support later if the child's needs require it, and a waiver of the child's rights is not binding. Visitation is enforced through the court, never by taking the child. The 20 to 30 percent of income figure that circulates online is not a statutory rule in India. Keep receipts for school fees, medical bills and travel, and record every missed visit.
